sentences.text: Thalattoarchon was a large predatory ichthyosaur that lived in North America during the Middle Triassic period.
This apex predator possessed large, robust teeth with two cutting edges that could reach up to 12 cm in length.
Its head featured elongated eye sockets reaching up to 29 cm, each containing a scleral ring.
Despite incomplete fossils, the animal is estimated to have had at least 60 presacral vertebrae.
While the original describing team estimated Thalattoarchon to be over 8.6 meters long, a 2023 book by Darren Naish revised this estimate to 9 meters.
The animal spent its entire life in the water and exhibited reduced bone ossification adapted to marine existence.
In 2021, researchers proposed that Thalattoarchon could have reached a body mass of 4.3 metric tons.
Thalattoarchon is recognized as the oldest known aquatic megapredator tetrapod in the fossil record, appearing four million years after the first appearance of ichthyosaurs.
Living eight million years after the Permian-Triassic mass extinction, its existence suggests that marine ecosystems recovered faster than terrestrial ones.
Thalattoarchon was described in 2013 based on a single partial skeleton found in Nevada, which was discovered in 1997 by paleontologist Jim Holstein in the Augusta Mountains.
In 2013, the specimen was designated the holotype for the new species Thalattoarchon saurophagis by a team including Nadia B. Fröbisch and Olivier Rieppel.
The fossils were completely exhumed in 2008 with support from the National Geographic Society after three weeks of work.
The known material consists of a partial skull, vertebrae, hip bones, and parts of the hind flippers.
Thalattoarchon was an active animal with a high metabolic rate that allowed it to maintain its body temperature.
Due to its apex predator adaptations, Thalattoarchon likely did not feed on ammonites, squid, or fish.
Researchers suggest Thalattoarchon may have fed only on smaller animals, living or dead, similar to a great white shark.

The classification of Thalattoarchon is debated, with it being placed either in the clade Merriamosauria or the basal family Cymbospondylidae, though Sander and colleagues reclassified it within Merriamosauria as the sister taxon to the Shastasauridae in 2021.
Thalattoarchon is classified in the class Reptilia.
The fossils date to approximately 244.6 million years ago, corresponding to the beginning of the late Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic.
Thalattoarchon was one of the most abundant marine reptiles found in the Fossil Hill Member.
It is debated whether Thalattoarchon hunted Cymbospondylus using a pack-hunting strategy, as this behavior is not reported in the fossil record.
